text.p: McLeodUSA Inc. has agreed to buy Consolidated Communications Inc., another telecommunications company, in a deal valued at about $420 million, the companies said Monday.

McLeodUSA, based in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, provides telecommunications services and competes with regional Baby Bell companies and GTE Corp., which have a virtual monopoly hold on local service in most parts of the country. Consolidated is a telecommunications holding company.
The combined company, McLeodUSA Inc., would have about 200,000 local lines, 4,000 employees and 3,700 miles of fiber optic lines in a 14-state region, and publish 12 million phone directories a year.
Annual sales would be about $400 million and earnings before interest, taxes and other items would be about $6 million, the companies said.
Under the agreement, owners of Consolidated Communications will receive 8.49 million shares of McLeodUSA stock, or a 13.9 percent stake in the company, and $155 million in cash.
McLeodUSA also will assume Consolidated's debt, which includes long-term debt of about $60 million.
Clark McLeod, chairman of McLeodUSA, said its strategy remains to first build market share, but added it can be accomplished faster through increased sales and marketing strength.
"Our second step is to build network," he added. "McLeodUSA has over 2,800 route miles of fiber optic network; CCI adds another 900 route miles to that total."

He said McLeodUSA plans to move customers to its own network and switches. That strategy is already being executed by Consolidated, with more than 15,000 competitive access lines, three local switching centres and two long distance switching centres, he added.
The companies said they expected to complete the merger, which was unanimously approved by the board of directors of each company, within a few months.
The deal is subject to approval by regulators. It does not require approval by McLeodUSA stockholders.

The owners of Consolidated have agreed to a pact with IES Industries Inc., MidAmerican Energy Co., and Clark and Mary McLeod. These parties have agreed to elect each other's representative to the board of directors of McLeodUSA and to restrict their sale of McLeodUSA stock for 12 months.
McLeod's stock rose $2.125 to $26.625 on Nasdaq.
